answer: Every identity needs a lantern lit to act, and a lantern eats quartz. A raven cuts that quartz from the claim the root holds, and the more a claim is cut the less it yields: a whole measure on the first cut, half on the second, a thousandth on the thousandth. So filling the thousandth lantern takes a thousand measures of raw quartz, and an operator holding a thousand lanterns burns five hundred thousand five hundred measures, while an honest newcomer burns one; no measure is shared. Ravens keep a ledger of every cut per root, so a fresh wallet still starts at the thousandth.
